facts.text: ManipArena-Sim is the simulation environment for the ManipArena bimanual manipulation benchmark, built on Isaac Lab and IsaacLab-Arena
SUPPORTED_SDK_ROBOTS lists quanta_x1, quanta_x2 and artixon_arm_6a
build_sdk_ros2_gym_env is documented to return (gym_env, embodiment) for the selected public SDK robot
The SDK ROS2 builder supports exactly one environment and raises when num_envs is not 1
sdk_simulation_timing defaults physics_dt to 1/120 s, decimation to 6 and render_interval to 2
The SDK builder assigns env_cfg.decimation = decimation before it makes the gym environment
AssembledEnvironment is documented to wrap a scene, an embodiment and a task into a lazily built gym environment
build_gym_environment calls gym.make(env_name, cfg=env_cfg, **env_kwargs).unwrapped and returns that environment
get_env builds the gym environment with build_gym_environment when it is not built yet and returns it
The builder configuration defaults the seed to 42 when the caller supplies none
The SDK launcher calls build_sdk_ros2_gym_env and then gym_env.reset()
The evaluation loop unpacks obs, _, terminated, truncated, _ = gym_env.step(actions), the Gymnasium five-tuple
The SDK runtime exposes robot state and either Cartesian or joint commands, without recording
The desktop SDK uses the fruit tabletop scene with an empty task and has no automatic timeout or success reset
The prerequisites are Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 with an NVIDIA GPU, Python 3.12, CUDA 12.8 and Isaac Sim 6.x binary wheels
The installer pins Isaac Sim to the wheels isaacsim[all,extscache]==6.0.1.0
The project dependencies are numpy, PyYAML, av, pyarrow, msgpack, msgpack-numpy and websockets, with no serial, VISA, USB or vendor hardware package
The quanta_x2 SDK guide states that ee is the default arm_control mode and that joint mode subscribes to joint commands instead
The artixon SDK guide gives the per-arm joint order as left_arm_joint1..6 and right_arm_joint1..6 and the angle unit as radians
The README states Apache License 2.0

determinism.notes: reset(seed=...) is forwarded to the Gymnasium environment and the fake seeds Python's random.Random; the upstream builder passes the seed to IsaacLab-Arena and Isaac Lab, which was not run, so a seed was never compared between the fake and the real simulator

gaps: kinematic F0 stand-in: no Isaac Sim physics, rigid bodies, contacts, actuators, sensors, noise or rendering; the fake advances one placeholder state coordinate per tick and claims no dynamics

the real action space is the batched Box of the configured embodiment and arm_control mode (the SDK supports quanta_x1, quanta_x2 and artixon_arm_6a, Cartesian or joint control), so its width and bounds depend on the payload; the fake uses a twelve-value placeholder Box and the conformance fixture uses that width, while the driver validates the live environment's shape at run time and invents no bound
the real observation is a Gymnasium Dict of observation-manager groups and camera images; the fake returns a four-value policy group only, so its arrays are smaller than the device's
the upstream environment is vectorized over num_envs (the SDK builder accepts exactly one) while this driver exposes one environment; the real stack was not executed
the upstream builder needs Isaac Sim 6.x wheels, Isaac Lab, IsaacLab-Arena, Linux and an NVIDIA GPU (README.md:36-44; docs/install.md:13); this package ships no sim backend and only the fake was run
timestep_ms 50.0 is physics_dt 1/120 s times the default decimation 6 (src/maniparena_sim/environment/sdk_builder.py:45-49 and :173); a different simulation payload changes it
snapshot and restore are not offered: the driver exposes no get_state/set_state
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and clock lockstep
